snippet.title: Evolution of Indian Flag.🇮🇳📊 #shorts #15august #indianflag #tiranga #flag #evolution #change #nation
snippet.description:
Evolution of Indian Flag.🇮🇳📊

The Indian national flag was changed (or modified) six times during various stages of the Indian independence movement before arriving at its present form. Its colors and symbols were changed from time to time to reflect the country's political identity and unity.

1* First flag (1906)

 7 August 1906 at Parsee Bagan Square, Kolkata and It had three horizontal stripes of green, yellow, and red. The top green stripe featured eight white lotus flowers, the middle yellow stripe featured "Vande Mataram," and the bottom red stripe featured a sun and crescent moon and This was an early attempt at national identity in the country during the Swadeshi movement.

2* Second flag (1907)

It was hoisted by Madame Bhikaji Cama at the International Socialist Conference in Germany (Stuttgart) in 1907 and This one, too, had three stripes (saffron/orange on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom). It also featured a lotus and the stars of the Big Dipper and Minor amendments were made to promote Indian independence and establish identity abroad.

3* Third flag (1917)

Hoisted by Dr. Annie Besant and Lokmanya Tilak during the Home Rule Movement and The flag had the British Union Jack in the corner, a crescent and star on one side, and seven stars diagonally representing the Big Dipper and  It reflected the political demand of the time (Dominion status within the British Raj).

*4 Fourth flag (1921)

During the Congress Committee session in Vijayawada and It was designed by a young man from Andhra Pradesh, Pingali Venkayya , and presented to Mahatma Gandhi. It featured two red and green stripes, symbolizing the two major communities. At Gandhi's suggestion, a white stripe was addedto represent the remaining communities and a spinning wheel , symbolizing the nation's progress and There was a need to bring together all the communities of the country and self-reliance.

5* Fifth flag (1931)

It was officially adopted by the Congress Party in the year 1931 and It featured saffron at the top (symbolizing courage), white in the middle (peace), and green at the bottom (prosperity), with Mahatma Gandhi's spinning wheel in the center. It was clarified that these colors had no communal connotation and The red colour was changed to saffron to promote communal harmony and give a clear national message.


6* Sixth and current tricolour (1947)

It was adopted as the national flag of independent India by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947 and The three colours of the 1931 flag (saffron, white, green) were retained, but the spinning wheel in the centre was replaced by Emperor Ashoka's Dharma Chakra (Ashoka Chakra) which has 24 spokes and The replacement of the spinning wheel with the chakra gave the country the eternal message of dynamism, justice and progress, which became the pride of the entire nation above any one party or symbol.
.
.
#independenceday #nationalflag #mahatmagandhi #freedomfighter #1947 #movement #british #country #india #indian #bharat

snippet.title: Evolution of Tank Armor
snippet.description:
Early tanks used riveted armor plates, but even when enemy shells failed to penetrate, the impact could shear rivets off inside the tank, turning them into deadly metal fragments. Engineers later switched to welded armor to remove this danger, but poor welding techniques sometimes trapped gas bubbles inside the metal, weakening the structure. Tanks then evolved with harder steel armor, leading to new anti-tank ammunition like HESH, or High Explosive Squash Head rounds. Instead of penetrating armor directly, HESH shells created spalling — breaking metal fragments off the inside wall of the tank and injuring the crew. This Shorts explains the constant evolution between tank armor and anti-tank weapons.
How did tank armor evolve from dangerous flying rivets to advanced steel plating, and why were HESH shells still deadly against it?

snippet.title: Pelé & Neymar: The Evolution of a Legendary Friendship (2010-2022) 🤝🇧🇷
snippet.description:
Experience the incredible friendship and bond between two Brazilian football legends, Pelé and Neymar 🇧🇷⚽. From Neymar’s early days at Santos to becoming one of the greatest stars of his generation, Pelé always admired and supported the young Brazilian talent.

This video shows their journey through the years, their memorable meetings, mutual respect, and the special connection between two generations of Brazilian football. From 2010 to 2022, witness how their friendship and football legacy evolved over time. ❤️👑
